# Check — M0-a-06, transactions: closing check of hardening round S7 (lane check/M0-a-06-close-s7, 2026-10-14)

**Verdict: PASS.** This checker re-ran the evidence of each of the round's 21 lines with its own probes and mutants.
Every line is either fixed and pinned, or left REPORTED with a stated reason: another item's owns, a registry row that
does not exist yet, or a case no family reaches. No new finding is a blocker.

* **Refusal census.** The registered families' counts are unchanged, and the wide families fall by 5 on this checker's
  own 52 220-batch golden.
* **R-10.** The nine index-freshness refusals of R-10 go to 0.
* **No shift outside R-10.** Everything in the round except R-10 is byte-identical to the pre-round sources over all
  52 220 batches.
* **Pins.** All 34 of this checker's targeted mutants were run; 31 are killed. The three survivors are M04 (equivalent),
  K16 (unreached in 138 620 batches, in both index modes) and Q57b (a 2 cm pad, PLAUSIBLE-equivalent on the lattice).

Four new findings go to the notes (`checks/M0-a-06-notes.md`, N-s7c-1 – N-s7c-4). The most important is **N-s7c-1**.
The round's new restoration trigger makes one lawful `remove lane` batch refuse that S6's order commits on the
identical arena. It is CONFIRMED, fail-safe, and appears once in 86 400 extra batches (0 in the registered and S6
families). It is routed to the session with RQ2.

Seat: closing checker, independent of the author (J162). No line in the lane log names this lane key, so the check
started fresh. This checker fixed its probe and mutant plan (34 targeted mutants, the goldens) before reading the
author's 'Hardening round S7' section, C-0361 and L-0530. It read them afterwards and judges them here; they are not
used as evidence. **Disclosure:** the first grep of the lane log for `M0-a-06` also printed the author's CHECKPOINT and
LANDED lines of lane `build/M0-a-06-fix-s7` before the plan was fixed. That was unavoidable for the RESUME check, and
they were not used as a map.

* **Machine and tools.** Machine id `linux:Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.80GHz:4cpu:16gib` (J198, matches); Node
  v24.12.0. `test_budget.py` printed 1 worker and 1 mutant slot. No timing was taken or gated on.
* **No git.** No git command was run. The pre-round sources came through the GitHub contents API (`gh api`).
* **Concurrent runs.** RELATED ran in the tree (1 worker) while this checker's goldens and mutants ran one at a time in
  its mirror (1 worker each), as the earlier closing checks of this item did.

## Method

* **Before-image.** `main` (`93837438`, an autosave) carries `src/tx` and `test/tx` as committed at `c4f10057` (round
  S6, the last commit touching `src/tx`). Fetching every file of both folders and comparing with the tree gives this
  diff:
  * `src/tx`: `index.ts` (comment), `relevel.ts`, `savepoint.ts`, `state.ts` and `tx.ts` differ.
  * `test/tx`: `chains`, `cost`, `forms`, `readable`, `removals`, `restore`, `savepoint` and `support` differ, and
    `hardening.test.ts` is new.
* **Mirrors** under `scratchpad/waves/check-M0-a-06/`. Each is a whole copy of `plat/` (no `dist`) with its own
  `node_modules` (`install --frozen-lockfile --offline`, exit 0; `@plat/*` resolve inside the copy).
  * `after`: the tree. `diff -rq` against the tree is clean before and after the sweep.
  * `pre`: `after` with `main`'s `src/tx` swapped in.

  Every mutant was applied by exact-string replacement, restored, and `cmp`-checked against the tree.
* **Probes** (scratch only, never in the tree):
  * `zz-check-s7-golden.test.ts`: fuzz.test.ts's generator and loop. Per batch it records the kind, the outcome (code
    and detail, or a throw), the sha of the record, the sha of `bits(p)` and of `contentPrint(p)`, `allProblems` +
    `checkIndexState`, `encodeArena` and `routeLines` of every chain, and, for a refusal, whether the state is
    unchanged. It runs in two modes: `fresh`, and `reattach` (`attachIndex` before every batch, as after a load).
  * The families: the registered ones (default ×7 919 and along ×104 729, seeds 1 – 24; the ten regressions) and the S6
    golden's wide families (default 1 – 1 200 @14, along 1 – 1 200 @16, heavy ×15 485 863 1 – 800 @20): 52 220
    batches. Also this checker's extra families: along and heavy ×999 983, ×1 299 709 and ×40 503, seeds 1 – 800:
    86 400 batches.
  * `zz-check-s7-r12`: R-12's rows inside the callback. `zz-check-s7-diag`: the vertex rows before a refused batch,
    with a flag-switched copy of restoration's trigger. `zz-check-s7-cost`: N-9's ratios on N-9's own multipliers.

  then the kerb's removal dissolves it', which is the declared shift. 40 titles are new.

## (3) New findings, judged by the blocker rule

No blocker. Notes appended to `checks/M0-a-06-notes.md` under "Hardening round S7 — the closing check's notes":

* **N-s7c-1** (LAWFUL, routed). The S7 trigger refuses heavy ×1 299 709 seed 1 @18 `remove lane`, which S6's order
  commits on the identical arena (CONFIRMED with a flag-switched trigger). The batch is fail-safe (nothing written). It
  appears once in 86 400 extra batches, and 0 times in the registered and S6 families.
* **N-s7c-2** (LAWFUL, routed, pre-existing). Two R-10-class refusals remain in the extra families, out of 25 before the
  round. Each involves a vertex between identical two-way rows, plausibly RQ2's.
* **N-s7c-3** (hardening). N-9's restated wide constant is exceeded on N-9's own multipliers (208; lane-heavy 298 and
  428).
* **N-s7c-4** (hardening). Q57b, a 2 cm pad, survives the Q57 pin.
